title: SettingsDialog is a 2,812-line god class bound together by stringly-typed control lookups
existing_state: SettingsDialog.cs is a single 2,812-line class containing six CreateXxxTab builder methods, two full profile-manager subsystems, the appearance preview engine, and one monolithic BtnSave_Click that writes ~60 settings across every tab (2657-2755). Its ~60 control fields are hydrated after construction by 34 recursive name-string lookups — FindControl<T>(tab, "chkRememberState") etc. (bindings from line 276) — where FindControl returns null! on a miss (2308-2317): renaming a control's Name string compiles cleanly and produces a NullReferenceException at first use, far from the cause, with zero compile-time safety. The form is hard-fixed at 544x620 FixedDialog (212-213) with dead resize anchors (223) — symptomatic of a class nobody can safely restructure. This is the same structure that let the Vault/Notification twins drift apart unnoticed (separate finding): with everything in one file there is no seam that forces shared behavior or per-tab review.
recommendation: Split each tab into a typed UserControl (controls assigned to fields directly at construction — delete FindControl entirely) exposing a small contract: Load(AppConfiguration), Apply(AppConfiguration), Validate(). SettingsDialog becomes a shell that composes the six tab controls and orchestrates Save by calling Validate/Apply in order inside one _configService.Update. Do it one tab at a time (General and Updates are trivial starters); the existing SettingsDialogVaultTests/AppearanceTests exercising the internal ctor keep the refactor honest.
user_benefit: Settings work stops being high-risk: new options become localized, compile-checked changes instead of edits to a 2,800-line form where a renamed string detonates at runtime — and it unblocks making the dialog resizable.
